title: AMD risk factors on impairment, acquisitions, debt covenants and geopolitical exposure
summary: This community is a set of risk factors from one AMD filing, grouped under economic and strategic, legal and regulatory, merger and acquisition, and general risks [0000002488-25-000166:0044]. The filing treats AMD as the accounting acquirer in its acquisitions, which left significant goodwill and intangible assets on its balance sheet [0000002488-25-000166:0077]. Its linked risks cover impairment charges, joint-venture dependence, debt covenants inherited from the Xilinx notes, and exposure to conflicts and disruption in Taiwan and China [0000002488-25-000166:0074].
findings: A deterioration in the long-term economic outlook or expected future cash flows could result in impairment charges, which may have a material adverse impact on AMD's financial position and results of operations [0000002488-25-000166:0077].
The majority of AMD's ATMP services are provided by the ATMP JVs, and there is no guarantee that the JVs will be able to fulfill its long-term ATMP requirements [0000002488-25-000166:0076].

AMD's unsecured Revolving Credit Agreement of $3.0 billion requires a minimum consolidated interest coverage ratio at the end of each fiscal quarter, and AMD guarantees Xilinx's 2.375% Notes due 2030 [0000002488-25-000166:0074].

Geopolitical changes between China and Taiwan could disrupt the operations of AMD's Taiwan-based third-party wafer foundries, manufacturing facilities and subcontractors [0000002488-25-000166:0079]. Nearly all product assembly and final testing is performed at third-party facilities in China, Malaysia and Taiwan [0000002488-25-000166:0078].
International sales were 64% of net revenue for the three months ended September 27, 2025, and AMD expects them to remain a significant portion of total sales [0000002488-25-000166:0078].

The market for qualified employees in AI and machine learning is highly competitive, and AMD relies on share-based incentive awards to attract and retain executives and employees [0000002488-25-000166:0080].
AMD has up to $14 billion authorized under its stock repurchase program, and $9.4 billion remained available as of September 27, 2025 [0000002488-25-000166:0081].

Some competitors are pursuing alternative computing architectures such as Arm, and customers may internally develop products for AI workloads similar to AMD's, which could reduce demand for its products [0000002488-25-000166:0044].

title: AMD operational risks: product quality, supply chain, outsourced logistics, gray market and IT systems
summary: This community groups operational and technology risk factors from AMD's 10-K, covering product compatibility, defects, supply chain efficiency, outsourced logistics, gray market sales and internal IT systems [0000002488-25-000166:0043]. The members share a theme: a failure in product quality, product delivery or internal systems could materially and adversely affect the business [0000002488-25-000166:0060] [0000002488-25-000166:0061]. The gray market risk names AMD directly and ties unauthorized sales to AMD's ethics, values and compliance standards [0000002488-25-000166:0060].
findings: AMD relies on third-party providers to operate its regional product distribution centers, manage transportation and provide IT support, and it cannot guarantee those providers will perform on time [0000002488-25-000166:0061].

The filing says the efficiency of AMD's supply chain becomes more important as it grows, and if it cannot deliver the right products on time, customers may reduce the quantities they order [0000002488-25-000166:0061].
Defects in products could lead to recall and replacement costs, loss of revenue, inventory write-downs, litigation and damage to AMD's reputation [0000002488-25-000166:0060].
The filing states that the mere announcement of an incompatibility problem with AMD's products could have a material adverse effect on its business [0000002488-25-000166:0060].

AMD says its internal information systems will continually change, and that these changes may be costly and disruptive, and that it is consolidating and standardizing systems [0000002488-25-000166:0059]. Its IT systems may also be vulnerable to cyberattacks, data breaches and outages, exposing it to significant cost [0000002488-25-000166:0060].

Gray market products may be counterfeit, substandard or used, may have higher failure rates, and create shadow inventory that AMD cannot see, making demand harder to forecast [0000002488-25-000166:0060] [0000002488-25-000166:0062].

title: Industry risk factors and the NVIDIA partnership
summary: This community is mostly a set of risk factors from one filing (0000002488-25-000166) covering demand, product transitions, customer concentration, cyclicality, economic uncertainty and intellectual property [0000002488-25-000166:0046]. That filing names Intel and NVIDIA as competitors and says NVIDIA's September 2025 partnership and investment in Intel may increase competition and pricing pressure [0000002488-25-000166:0045]. The community also links to Intel's own filing (0000050863-26-000011), which describes a strategic partnership with NVIDIA to co-develop custom client and data center products [0000050863-26-000011:0007].

The filing warns that delays in developing or shipping new products may cause it to miss customers' design windows, and that product prices decline over a product's life, so new products are needed to maintain average selling prices [0000002488-25-000166:0048].
The filing describes the semiconductor industry as highly cyclical and says it has incurred substantial losses in previous downturns [0000002488-25-000166:0045].

Intel says its NVIDIA partnership is intended to jointly develop multiple generations of products for hyperscale, enterprise and consumer markets based on the x86 architecture [0000050863-26-000011:0007].

title: Third-party dependencies: Microsoft, AIB partners, distributors and component suppliers
summary: The passages come from a single AMD filing, which names AMD Instinct MI308 products [0000002488-25-000166:0057]. The risks are linked because each says a loss or failure of one of these outside parties could materially affect AMD's business [0000002488-25-000166:0058] [0000002488-25-000166:0059].
findings: AMD says its ability to innovate beyond the x86 instruction set depends partly on Microsoft designing its operating systems to run on or support AMD's x86-based microprocessors and graphics products [0000002488-25-000166:0058].

Some software drivers licensed for use with AMD's x86 products are certified by Microsoft, and AMD says that if Microsoft did not certify a driver, its ability to market x86 products would be materially adversely affected [0000002488-25-000166:0059].

AMD depends on third-party companies for the design, manufacture and supply of motherboards, graphics cards, software, memory and other components, and it also relies on its AIB partners to support its products [0000002488-25-000166:0058].

AMD's agreements with distributors and AIB partners can generally be terminated for convenience on prior notice and are non-exclusive, permitting them to offer competitors' products [0000002488-25-000166:0059].

AMD states that if a significant distributor or AIB partner terminated its relationship or decided not to market AMD products, its ability to bring products to market would be affected and it would be materially adversely affected [0000002488-25-000166:0059].

AMD's agreements with AIB partners protect their inventory against price reductions, so a significant decline in product prices would reduce AMD's revenue and gross margin [0000002488-25-000166:0059].

AMD relies on third-party intellectual property and development tools, and AMD says that if such intellectual property becomes unavailable or fails to meet requirements, its business could be materially adversely affected [0000002488-25-000166:0058].

AMD says forecasting demand is further complicated when its products are sold indirectly through downstream channel distributors, because forecasts then rely on estimates from multiple parties [0000002488-25-000166:0057].

title: AMD operational, cyber and third-party supply risk factors

AMD relies on third-party intellectual property such as development and testing tools, and if that IP becomes unavailable or lacks required functionality, its business could be materially adversely affected [0000002488-24-000056:0046].

title: AMD acquisition, debt covenant and worldwide operations risks
summary: The passages tie these risks to the Xilinx and Pensando acquisitions, with AMD named as the accounting acquirer [0000002488-24-000123:0070]. The community also covers AI-related reputational and regulatory risk [0000002488-24-000123:0066].
findings: AMD unconditionally guarantees, on a senior unsecured basis, Xilinx's obligations under its 2.375% Notes, which are the Assumed Xilinx Notes [0000002488-24-000123:0067].

The indenture for AMD's 3.924% Senior Notes due 2032 and 4.393% Senior Notes due 2052, and the supplemental indenture for the Assumed Xilinx Notes, limit AMD's ability to create certain liens, enter sale and leaseback transactions, and merge or sell substantially all assets [0000002488-24-000123:0067].

AMD's $3.0 billion unsecured Revolving Credit Agreement requires a minimum consolidated interest coverage ratio at each fiscal quarter end, and cross-default provisions could let lenders accelerate borrowings [0000002488-24-000123:0067]. AMD cannot assure that it would have sufficient assets to repay accelerated borrowings [0000002488-24-000123:0068].

The majority of AMD's ATMP services are provided by the ATMP JVs, and there is no guarantee the JVs will fulfill AMD's long-term ATMP requirements [0000002488-24-000123:0069]. Late or fluctuating supply from the JVs could cause lost sales [0000002488-24-000123:0069].
Acquisitions may dilute stockholders' ownership, add debt or contingent liabilities, and cause amortization expenses and write-downs of acquired assets [0000002488-24-000123:0068].

AMD recorded significant goodwill and other intangible assets from the Xilinx and Pensando acquisitions, and future impairment charges could have a material adverse impact on its financial position and results of operations [0000002488-24-000123:0070].

International sales were 60% of AMD's net revenue for the three months ended June 29, 2024 [0000002488-24-000123:0071]. AMD relies on third-party wafer foundries in the United States, Europe and Asia, and nearly all product assembly and final testing is performed in China, Malaysia and Taiwan [0000002488-24-000123:0071].

AMD states that geopolitical changes between China and Taiwan could disrupt its Taiwan-based third-party wafer foundries, and that its Taiwan foundries were located where an April 2024 earthquake occurred [0000002488-24-000123:0072].

title: AMD export controls, US-China trade and tax risk
summary: This community concerns AMD's export control, US-China trade and tax risk factors, centered on EAR and ITAR licensing rules and the restrictions on advanced AI chips [0000002488-24-000123:0060]. The filings say AMD must keep compliance programs to meet EAR and ITAR requirements, and that licenses may not be granted in time or at all [0000002488-24-000123:0060][0000002488-25-000047:0056]. The tax risk factors cover deferred tax asset realization and global minimum tax rules such as Pillar Two [0000002488-26-000018:0046].
findings: AMD states that the United States has imposed unilateral controls restricting GPUs and associated products, and that these controls may prohibit exports to any or all customers in one or more markets, including China [0000002488-24-000123:0060].

Under BIS requirements issued in October 2023, AMD needs a license before shipping certain Instinct integrated circuits and Versal FPGAs to China, and must file a Notified Advanced Computing notification 25 days before shipping certain Versal FPGAs [0000002488-24-000163:0059].
AMD says it has no assurance that BIS will grant licenses or act on filings in a timely manner, and that a granted license may carry burdensome conditions [0000002488-24-000123:0060].

AMD cites US-China trade relations as uncertain because the United States keeps adding Chinese companies to the Entity List, and notes that China has imposed retaliatory tariffs [0000002488-25-000047:0056].

A September 2025 BIS rule covering entities at least 50% owned by listed parties was suspended for one year in October 2025, but the restrictions can be reimposed at any time [0000002488-26-000018:0045].
AMD warns that if it cannot realize its deferred tax assets, it could record a material expense that adversely affects its financial condition and results of operations [0000002488-24-000123:0060].

AMD reports that the OECD released a side-by-side package in January 2026 that exempts US-based multinationals from parts of the global minimum tax, but each country must adopt it before it is enacted for financial accounting purposes [0000002488-26-000018:0046].

title: AMD export controls, China restrictions and climate risk
summary: This community centers on AMD's export-control exposure, especially limits on shipping AMD Instinct integrated circuits and Versal FPGAs to China and other D5 Countries [0000002488-25-000047:0053]. It also groups AMD's climate-related risk factors, which cover supply chain disruption, supplier costs and insurance coverage [0000002488-25-000012:0041]. The same export-control and climate language recurs across several AMD filings [0000002488-25-000047:0053][0000002488-25-000166:0063].
findings: Since October 2023, BIS has required licenses before AMD ships certain Instinct integrated circuits and Versal FPGAs to China, or to customers outside the United States whose ultimate parent is headquartered in a D5 Country [0000002488-25-000047:0053].

In April 2025 the U.S. government required a license for certain semiconductor exports to D5 Countries, which affects the AMD Instinct MI308 products, and AMD incurred approximately $800 million in inventory and related charges in the second quarter of 2025 [0000002488-25-000166:0063].

In August 2025 U.S. government officials said they expected to receive 15% of the revenue from licensed MI308 sales to China, but no regulation establishing this has been published [0000002488-25-000166:0064].

BIS announced in May 2025 that it intends to rescind the January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule and issue replacement rules, which may limit AMD's transactions, require new licenses or delay shipments [0000002488-25-000166:0064].
AMD is subject to the Export Administration Regulations, which restrict exports of certain products and technologies to countries including China, Russia and Belarus [0000002488-25-000166:0063].
AMD holds equity interests in two joint ventures with Higon Information Technology, and BIS added THATIC and the THATIC JV to the Entity List in June 2019 [0000002488-25-000012:0042].

AMD states that supply chain delays from climate-related disruptions may lead to contractual disputes, litigation and higher costs, and that data centers' dependence on water and energy could reduce customer purchases [0000002488-26-000018:0041].
AMD's insurance policies have large deductibles and broad exclusions, and losses not covered by insurance could materially harm its results [0000002488-25-000012:0042].

title: Intel cybersecurity threats, supply-chain attacks and data privacy rules
summary: This community covers Intel's cybersecurity and data privacy risk disclosures, which tie attacks on its products, services and supply chain to the laws and standards it must follow [0000050863-25-000009:0065]. It names the 2020 SolarWinds compromise and the 2024 CrowdStrike outage as supply-chain examples, and the Habana Labs subsidiary network breach as a direct incident [0000050863-25-000009:0065]. The cybersecurity risk wording recurs in Intel's 2024 and 2025 filings [0000050863-25-000009:0081] [0000050863-26-000011:0078].
findings: Intel says its Habana Labs subsidiary network was breached in the fourth quarter of 2020 in connection with a suspected unsuccessful ransomware attack, resulting in unauthorized third-party access to certain confidential information [0000050863-25-000009:0065].
Intel reports that since 2021 it has observed an increase in ransomware attacks in its supply chain [0000050863-25-000009:0065].

Intel's cybersecurity risk section cites the breadth of its geographies, networks and systems, and the attractiveness of its products to threat actors including state-sponsored organizations [0000050863-25-000009:0081].

Intel states that failure to comply with cybersecurity and data privacy laws, or a security compromise exposing personal information, may require it to modify or cease operations, incur substantial costs, or face legal proceedings or governmental investigations [0000050863-25-000009:0065].

Intel says there is increasing regulation of responses to cybersecurity incidents, including reporting to regulators, which could subject it to additional liability and reputational harm [0000050863-25-000009:0081].

Intel expects its foundry business and its cloud and SaaS offerings to collect significant amounts of highly sensitive customer data, which may make it a target of attempts to steal or corrupt that data [0000050863-25-000009:0064].

Intel states that, as of the date of its 2025 Form 10-K, it had not experienced a cybersecurity threat or incident with a material adverse impact on its business or operations, but it cannot guarantee it will not in the future [0000050863-26-000011:0092].

Intel's Board of Directors has ultimate oversight of cybersecurity risk, and the Audit & Finance Committee reviews the cybersecurity program with management, generally at least twice annually [0000050863-26-000011:0092].

title: Data privacy, cross-border transfer and cyber-risk regulation
summary: This community centers on risk factors about personal data privacy, cross-border data transfers and cyberattacks, tied to regulations such as the GDPR, the CCPA, NIS2, the EU AI Act and China's data rules [0001045810-25-000023:0048]. The passages come from two filers, one under ID 0001045810 and one under ID 0000002488, and they describe the same regulatory exposures, though the filer names are not stated in the text [0000002488-24-000163:0051].
findings: The GDPR allows penalties of up to €20 million or 4% of worldwide revenue, whichever is greater, and the filing warns that consumer protection organizations may bring litigation over personal data processing [0001045810-26-000021:0049].
Under NIS2, non-compliance may lead to administrative fines of up to 10 million Euros or 2% of total worldwide revenue of the preceding fiscal year [0001045810-26-000021:0050].
China's law may bar transfer of important data, including personal data, outside China without prior assessment and approval by the Cyberspace Administration of China [0001045810-26-000021:0050].

The Standard Contractual Clauses are one mechanism for moving personal data out of the EEA, but the filing notes these mechanisms are subject to legal challenges and there is no assurance they can be relied on [0001045810-25-000023:0049].

The CCPA gives California residents rights to access, delete and opt out of certain sharing of personal information, and it provides for substantial fines for intentional violations and a private right of action for certain data breaches [0001045810-25-000023:0048].

AMD's 2024 filing said an AI act was being considered in the EU [0000002488-24-000123:0065], while its 2025 filing says the EU AI Act was adopted in 2024 and will be phased in over the next few years [0000002488-25-000047:0061].

Compromised user access credentials, obtained through phishing, vishing, MFA prompt bombing or social engineering, can let cyberattacks into IT systems, which could lead to reputational harm, loss of customers, litigation and significant remediation costs [0000002488-24-000163:0051].

title: Responsible AI, IP litigation and sustainability scrutiny risks

title: Environmental, forced-labor and data-privacy compliance risks
summary: The passages come from two filings that share the filer prefix 0000002488, and they do not name the company [0000002488-25-000012:0047] [0000002488-25-000166:0070]. findings: The company has been named a responsible party at three Superfund sites in Sunnyvale, California, and it is subject to Final Site Clean-up Requirements Orders from the California Regional Water Quality Control Board [0000002488-25-000012:0047]. It has settled with other responsible parties on two of those orders, but it remains liable for costs beyond the settlements and for all remaining costs if the other parties do not fulfill their obligations [0000002488-25-000012:0047].

Environmental laws are described as complex, changing frequently and tending to become more stringent over time [0000002488-25-000012:0048]. The EU and China have restricted lead and other materials in electronic products, and these rules affect semiconductor devices and packaging [0000002488-25-000012:0048].

Non-compliance by manufacturing suppliers could result in disruptions in supply, higher sourcing costs and reputational damage for the company [0000002488-25-000166:0070]. Governments and customers are focused on eliminating forced labor in supply chains, which may increase the cost of the company's compliance program [0000002488-25-000166:0071]. Failure to meet customer expectations on forced and trafficked labor policies may cause customers to choose a competitor's product or lead to enforcement liability [0000002488-25-000166:0072].

Many governments have enacted personal data laws such as the GDPR and the CCPA, and failure to comply could result in sanctions [0000002488-25-000166:0072]. The GDPR also imposes significant requirements on how personal data is collected, processed and transferred, along with significant fines for non-compliance [0000002488-25-000166:0072].

California has passed reporting requirements that will require corporations to report on climate data, and these laws include third-party verification requirements [0000002488-25-000012:0049]. The company says failure to comply, or the appearance of failure to comply, can result in regulatory penalties, fines and legal liabilities [0000002488-25-000012:0049].

The EU AI Act was adopted in 2024 and will be phased in over the next few years, and similar legislation is being considered in other jurisdictions [0000002488-25-000012:0049]. The company expects this regulatory environment to increase the cost of doing business and create compliance risks and potential liability [0000002488-25-000012:0049].

title: AMD Sunnyvale Superfund sites and environmental liability
summary: AMD has been named a responsible party for three Superfund sites in Sunnyvale, California on the National Priorities List, and this community centers on remediation of those sites under orders from the California Regional Water Quality Control Board [0000002488-26-000018:0018]. The filings tie these cleanup obligations to the Superfund Act and to a growing set of product environmental rules covering materials, energy and electronic waste [0000002488-26-000018:0019]. The passages all come from AMD's filings and none concern NVIDIA or Intel [0000002488-25-000166:0070].
findings: AMD recorded an estimated environmental liability of about $5.5 million for the orders and has not recorded any potential insurance recoveries in estimating the cleanup costs [0000002488-25-000012:0018].
In the later filing the recorded estimate rose to about $5.9 million, and AMD states that any amount beyond what is already accrued would not be material [0000002488-26-000018:0019].

The settlement arrangements changed between the two filings: the 2025 filing describes settlement agreements with other responsible parties on two of the orders [0000002488-25-000012:0018]. The 2026 filing describes a single agreement covering one site, under which the other party is responsible for certain offsite contamination [0000002488-26-000018:0019].

Under the Superfund Act, owners or operators of real property can face strict or joint and several liability for cleanup costs, often even without knowledge of the release [0000002488-25-000012:0018].

Electronic waste recycling and extended producer responsibility rules in the EU, China, Brazil, India, California and Sao Paulo require labeling, fees or reporting, and their scope is inconsistent, which increases compliance complexity [0000002488-26-000018:0019].

AMD's risk factors warn that noncompliance by its suppliers with environmental permit requirements could cause supply disruptions, higher sourcing costs and reputational damage [0000002488-25-000166:0070].
AMD says it could be named a potentially responsible party at other Superfund or contaminated sites in the future [0000002488-25-000166:0070].

title: Intel 14A external foundry dependence and manufacturing footprint
summary: This community centers on Intel's Intel 14A process node and whether it can be economically developed without a significant external foundry customer [0000050863-26-000011:0008]. Intel's filings say that if it cannot secure such a customer, it may pause or discontinue Intel 14A and successor leading-edge nodes, and a 10-Q describes that decision as potentially effectively irreversible [0000050863-26-000011:0034] [0000050863-25-000109:0065]. The same filings tie these choices to a streamlined manufacturing footprint, including the consolidation of Costa Rican assembly and test operations and the slowed Ohio fab and cancelled Germany and Poland projects [0000050863-26-000011:0008].
findings: Intel says it has few external foundry customers to date, while developing an external foundry business is a key long-term strategy [0000050863-26-000011:0008].

Intel states that if it discontinued development of Intel 14A and successor nodes, a majority of its products would continue to be manufactured in its own facilities on nodes up to Intel 18A-P through at least 2030 [0000050863-26-000011:0034].
Intel says that in such a case it would over time shift manufacturing to third-party foundries, particularly TSMC, for products on nodes beyond Intel 18A and Intel 18A-P [0000050863-26-000011:0008].
Intel 14A is described as its first node designed from inception for offering to external customers, and it may use high-NA EUV lithography [0000050863-26-000011:0021].
Intel 18A went into high-volume manufacturing in late 2025 and is used for the first Intel Core Ultra Series 3 processor [0000050863-26-000011:0021].
Intel shifted high-volume production of its Intel 4 and Intel 3 nodes to Ireland, while the Ohio fab is being built and plans for a Germany fab are on hold [0000050863-25-000009:0014].
Intel initiated the consolidation of its Costa Rican assembly and test operations into larger existing sites in Vietnam and Malaysia [0000050863-26-000011:0034].

title: Intel fabs, assembly sites and advanced packaging products
summary: The passages describe Intel alone, and no relationships among the members are listed, so the links are inferred from the same filings rather than stated as direct ties. [0000050863-26-000011:0022] [0000050863-25-000009:0014]
findings: Intel's 2025 key production fabs were in Oregon (ramping Intel 18A), Arizona (Intel 7 and ramping Intel 18A), Ireland (Intel 4 and Intel 3) and Israel (Intel 7) [0000050863-26-000011:0022].

title: Intel Core, Xeon 6, Gaudi 3 and software stack
summary: This community is about Intel's CPU product lines, its Gaudi 3 AI accelerators and its open software tools, all named in Intel's filings [0000050863-25-000009:0012]. The client, data center and AI products are tied together through shared process nodes, such as Intel 7, Intel 4 and Intel 3, which several of them are manufactured on [0000050863-26-000011:0020]. The community concerns only Intel; AMD and NVIDIA appear in the filings only as competitors [0000050863-25-000009:0024].
findings: Intel launched the Gaudi 3 AI accelerators in 2024, offering significant price-performance advantages for AI inference applications [0000050863-25-000009:0012]. The filings describe them as an AI accelerator line with enhanced memory bandwidth, flexibility and AI compute capabilities [0000050863-25-000009:0024].

Intel announced the Xeon 6 processor with Performance-cores together with the Gaudi 3 AI accelerator as its next-generation AI solutions [0000050863-24-000149:0006]. Its P-cores are hyperthreaded and have built-in matrix engines aimed at compute-intensive workloads such as AI [0000050863-25-000009:0024].

The OpenVINO toolkit is an open source toolkit that accelerates deep learning inference on Intel processors, and the filings call it the leading inferencing library on Intel silicon [0000050863-25-000009:0012].

Intel contributed its oneAPI specifications and implementations to the UXL Foundation under the Linux Foundation, and most of Intel's frameworks and middleware are built from oneAPI [0000050863-25-000009:0012].

Intel launched the Open Platform for Enterprise AI under the Linux Foundation in 2024 to accelerate deployment of generative AI use cases through a modular microservice architecture [0000050863-25-000009:0012].

Intel Xeon 6 processors are manufactured on the Intel 3 node, and the Intel Core Ultra Series 1 is manufactured on Intel 4 [0000050863-26-000011:0020]. The Intel Xeon 6 family was the first Intel Xeon processor line to use E-cores [0000050863-25-000009:0011].

Intel Core Ultra Series 1 introduced the first AI PCs to the market in 2023 [0000050863-26-000011:0014]. The 13th and 14th Gen Intel Core processors, made on Intel 7, represented almost half of Intel's client product sales in 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0014].

Intel said it was developing Falcon Shores as its next AI accelerator to succeed Gaudi but would use it as an internal test chip rather than bring it to market, and it is now focusing on Jaguar Shores [0000050863-25-000009:0024].

title: Intel forward-looking risk factors: competition, investment, supply chain and cybersecurity
summary: This community is a set of risk factors from Intel's Form 10-Q that the company says could cause actual results to differ materially from its forward-looking statements [0000050863-24-000076:0002]. The risks center on intense competition and rapid technological change, large long-term R&D and manufacturing investments, and the complexities of developing new semiconductor products and process technologies [0000050863-24-000076:0003]. The list also covers supply chain disruption, cybersecurity, currency exchange rates, debt and capital access, and the evolving market for AI products, and it concerns Intel only, not NVIDIA or AMD [0000050863-24-000076:0003].
findings: Intel lists the high level of competition and rapid technological change in its industry, and it warns that its significant long-term, inherently risky investments in R&D and manufacturing facilities may not realize a favorable return [0000050863-24-000076:0002].
Intel flags its ability to time and scale capital investments appropriately and to secure favorable alternative financing arrangements and government grants as a risk [0000050863-24-000076:0003].
The filing names its complex global supply chain as a risk, including disruptions, delays, trade tensions and conflicts, or shortages [0000050863-24-000076:0003].
Intel cites increasing and evolving cybersecurity threats, privacy risks, and potential security vulnerabilities in its products as risks [0000050863-24-000076:0003].
Intel lists its debt obligations and its ability to access sources of capital, along with fluctuations in currency exchange rates, as risks [0000050863-24-000076:0003].
The filing identifies the evolving market for products with AI capabilities and the need to attract, retain, and motivate key talent as risks [0000050863-24-000076:0003].
Intel points readers to other risks described in this report, its 2023 Form 10-K, and its other SEC filings, so this list is not exhaustive [0000050863-24-000076:0003].

title: Market risk disclosures: interest rate, equity price and foreign exchange exposure
summary: This community groups the market risk sections of the filings, covering investment and interest rate risk, publicly-held equity price risk and foreign exchange rate risk [0001045810-25-000023:0074]. The annual market risk disclosures for fiscal years 2025 and 2026 report fixed-rate senior Notes of $8.5 billion and an exposure to foreign currency that the filer calls minimal [0001045810-26-000021:0073]. A quarterly report on Form 10-Q for October 2025 states that there were no material changes to the foreign exchange risks described in the prior annual report [0001045810-25-000230:0048].
findings: The fiscal 2025 annual report says a parallel shift of plus or minus 0.5% in the yield curve would change the fair value of the investment portfolio by $238 million [0001045810-25-000023:0074].

title: Market risk disclosures: interest rate, default, investment and FX risk
summary: This community is the Item 7A market risk section of two annual filings from the same filer, covering interest rate, default, long-term investment and foreign exchange risk [0000002488-25-000012:0079]. The later filing's passages report larger exposures than the earlier one, including investment holdings and forward contract notional amounts [0000002488-26-000018:0083] [0000002488-26-000018:0084].
findings: A hypothetical 50 basis-point change in interest rates would have affected the fair value of the cash equivalent and investment portfolio by about $6 million as of December 28, 2024, and by about $25 million as of December 27, 2025 [0000002488-25-000012:0079] [0000002488-26-000018:0083].

All outstanding long-term debt carried fixed interest rates at both year-ends, so exposure to rate changes on reported interest expense was described as minimal [0000002488-25-000012:0079] [0000002488-26-000018:0083].
Default risk is limited by investing only in high credit quality securities, and all debt investments were A-rated by at least one rating agency as of December 27, 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0083].

A new long-term investment risk category was reported in the later filing, with publicly traded equity holdings of $198 million and non-marketable equity securities and other instruments of $1.3 billion as of December 27, 2025, against $0 and $468 million a year earlier [0000002488-26-000018:0083].

The aggregate notional amount of foreign currency forward contracts rose from $2.8 billion at December 28, 2024 to $3.4 billion at December 27, 2025, and the estimated net fair-value position moved from a $66 million loss to a $12 million gain [0000002488-26-000018:0084].

title: Intel x86 and xPU product strategy
summary: This community centers on Intel's x86 architecture and its xPU product family, which the company names as the core of its product competitiveness priority [0000050863-25-000009:0005]. findings: Intel describes the x86 ecosystem as the core of its business and says it has served as a foundation of modern computing for over four decades [0000050863-25-000009:0006].

title: AMD risk factors: Intel and Nvidia competition, supply chain, debt and legal exposure
summary: This community is a set of risk factors from AMD's 10-K and 10-Q filings, covering competition with Intel and Nvidia, supply chain and third-party dependence, customer concentration, and legal, environmental and debt exposure [0000002488-25-000012:0020][0000002488-26-000018:0022]. The filings say Intel's and Nvidia's dominance may limit AMD's ability to compete, and that AMD relies on third-party wafer foundries, assembly sites and distribution providers [0000002488-25-000012:0022][0000002488-26-000018:0058]. Several members also note reliance on Microsoft and other software vendors for x86 products and on a small number of customers for a substantial part of revenue [0000002488-25-000108:0059][0000002488-25-000012:0028].
findings: Intel's aggressive pricing, rebating and incentives have in the past resulted in lower unit sales and a lower average selling price for many AMD products, adversely affecting its margins and profitability [0000002488-25-000012:0022].
AMD states that Nvidia's practices can limit customers' ability to choose non-Nvidia products, including AMD's, which may limit its market share and decrease its margins [0000002488-25-000012:0022].

The filing says AMD's ability to market x86 products would be materially adversely affected if Microsoft does not keep designing its operating systems to work with those instruction sets, or if it loses software-vendor support [0000002488-25-000108:0059].

A small number of customers is expected to continue to account for a substantial part of AMD's revenue, and the loss of a key customer would materially adversely affect its business [0000002488-25-000012:0028].

AMD says it has been named a responsible party at three Superfund sites in Sunnyvale, California, and is subject to Final Site Clean-up Requirements Orders from the California Regional Water Quality Control Board [0000002488-26-000018:0049].

AMD unconditionally guarantees Xilinx's 2.375% Notes due 2030, and its $3.0 billion Revolving Credit Agreement requires a minimum consolidated interest coverage ratio at the end of each fiscal quarter [0000002488-26-000018:0053].
Gray market products are sold outside AMD's authorized channels and create shadow inventory that AMD cannot see, which makes demand harder to forecast [0000002488-25-000012:0041].
International sales were 67% of AMD's net revenue for the year ended December 27, 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0058].

title: NVIDIA export controls, H20 China licensing and related trade risk
summary: This community groups NVIDIA's filings on U.S. export controls and licensing, centered on H20 restrictions for China and the revenue, inventory and regulatory effects that followed [0001045810-25-000209:0034] [0001045810-25-000230:0063]. The reports concern NVIDIA only and do not describe AMD or Intel [0001045810-25-000209:0034]. The filings also describe Chinese regulatory responses, including an antitrust preliminary finding and questions about H20 vulnerabilities [0001045810-25-000230:0060] [0001045810-25-000230:0063].
findings: NVIDIA recorded a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations after the USG said a license was required for H20 exports into China [0001045810-25-000209:0034].

Under licenses granted in August 2025, NVIDIA generated approximately $50 million in H20 revenue, and U.S. officials expect to receive 15% of licensed sales, which has not been codified in a regulation [0001045810-25-000230:0062] [0001045810-25-000209:0054].

On September 15, 2025, China's antitrust regulators preliminarily found that NVIDIA's compliance with U.S. export controls discriminated unfairly against Chinese customers and violated the terms of China's approval of the Mellanox acquisition [0001045810-25-000230:0060].
Restrictions on selling data center GPUs may also reduce demand for NVIDIA's networking products used in servers containing its GPUs [0001045810-25-000230:0063].

A substantial portion of NVIDIA's products are warehoused in and distributed from Hong Kong, so export controls on gaming GPUs could disrupt a significant portion of its supply and distribution chain [0001045810-25-000116:0049].
The USG said in May 2025 that it would rescind the AI Diffusion IFR and replace it with a rule whose scope remains uncertain [0001045810-25-000230:0035] [0001045810-25-000209:0035].
NVIDIA says its competitive position has been harmed by export controls and could be further harmed if customers buy from competitors or develop internal solutions [0001045810-25-000209:0054].

title: NVIDIA market platforms, demand and supply risk, export controls and derivative suits
summary: This community concerns NVIDIA's market platforms, products and risk disclosures, including demand forecasting and supply-demand mismatch, Blackwell yield and inventory issues, export controls, and shareholder derivative litigation [0001045810-24-000264:0034] [0001045810-25-000116:0041]. findings: NVIDIA states that demand estimates for its products, applications, and services can be incorrect, which may create volatility in its revenue or supply levels [0001045810-25-000116:0044].

New unilateral export controls can be imposed after a product is ready for market, which may cause excess inventory and purchase obligations, as NVIDIA recently experienced with the H20 [0001045810-25-000116:0050].

In the second quarter of fiscal year 2026, Customer A represented 23% of total revenue and Customer B represented 16%, both attributable to the Compute & Networking segment [0001045810-25-000209:0039].

Cryptocurrency mining has made NVIDIA's demand hard to estimate, and reduced Ethereum mining after the Ethereum 2.0 merge created aftermarket sales that could reduce demand for new GPUs [0001045810-25-000023:0025].

Huang derivative actions in the District of Delaware were stayed until final resolution of the securities litigation [0001045810-25-000116:0021].

title: AMD acquisitions, ZT Systems sale, OpenAI agreement and supply chain risks
summary: This community centers on AMD's acquisitions of Xilinx, Pensando and Silo AI, and on the ZT Systems deal, including the sale of its manufacturing business to Sanmina [0000002488-25-000012:0101] [0000002488-25-000108:0079]. It also covers AMD's risk factors on competition from Intel and Nvidia, dependence on Microsoft and third-party suppliers, and product and supply chain exposures [0000002488-24-000163:0038] [0000002488-24-000163:0055]. The passages concern AMD, and the cited filings are AMD's own 10-K and 10-Q filings [0000002488-24-000163:0070].
findings: AMD completed the Xilinx acquisition on February 14, 2022 for a total purchase consideration of $48.8 billion, allocating $22.8 billion to goodwill [0000002488-25-000012:0101].
AMD completed the Silo AI acquisition on August 9, 2024, in an all-cash transaction of $665 million [0000002488-24-000163:0012].

AMD sold the ZT Manufacturing Business to Sanmina Corporation on October 27, 2025, for 1,151,052 shares of Sanmina common stock and $2.4 billion in cash, with up to $450 million more contingent on conditions [0000002488-25-000166:0030]. AMD retained the ZT Design Business [0000002488-26-000018:0005].

AMD entered into a product purchase agreement with OpenAI OpCo, LLC to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs, with the first gigawatt powered by AMD Instinct MI450 series products [0000002488-26-000018:0072].

The filing says Intel's aggressive pricing and incentives have in the past resulted in lower unit sales and a lower average selling price for many products, and Nvidia's practices can limit customers' ability to choose non-Nvidia products [0000002488-24-000163:0038] [0000002488-24-000163:0039].

title: Intel forward-looking risk factors: supply chain, geopolitics and capital investment
summary: This community groups Intel's risk-factor disclosures from its 10-K and 10-Q filings, covering geopolitics, supply chain, product quality, capital investment and financing [0000050863-25-000179:0002] [0000050863-25-000109:0003]. Its members concern Intel alone, and the passages do not name NVIDIA or AMD [0000050863-25-000179:0003]. The risks are tied to Intel's plans for Intel 14A, its manufacturing and supply in Israel and Taiwan, and its dependence on outside suppliers such as ASML and TSMC [0000050863-25-000109:0042] [0000050863-25-000009:0058] [0000050863-25-000009:0061] [0000050863-26-000011:0076].
findings: Intel says it could pause or discontinue its pursuit of Intel 14A and other next-generation leading-edge process technologies if it cannot secure a significant external customer for Intel 14A [0000050863-25-000179:0002].
Intel names its complex global supply chain, which includes external foundries, as exposed to disruptions, delays, trade tensions, conflicts or shortages [0000050863-25-000179:0003].

Intel names US-China trade tensions, Russia's war on Ukraine, tensions affecting Israel and the Middle East, and rising tensions between mainland China and Taiwan as macroeconomic risks [0000050863-25-000179:0002].

ASML is the sole supplier of EUV lithography tools that Intel deploys in its Intel 4 and subsequent leading-edge nodes, and delays in those tools could delay the ramp of future nodes [0000050863-25-000009:0061].
During 2024, some customers experienced instability issues with Intel Core 13th and 14th Gen desktop processors, which adversely affected 2024 sales volume [0000050863-26-000011:0076].

Intel says its Israel fabrication facility produces Intel 7 products that generate a significant portion of its revenue, and that it is not insured for business interruptions from war or political violence [0000050863-25-000109:0042].

Sales outside the US accounted for 76% of Intel's revenue in fiscal 2024, with billings to China at 29%, and for fiscal 2025 those figures were 70% and 24% [0000050863-25-000009:0056] [0000050863-26-000011:0071].

Intel says its significant long-term investments in R&D and manufacturing may not realize a favorable return, and it has significantly reduced its return of capital in recent years [0000050863-25-000109:0002] [0000050863-25-000179:0003].

title: AMD foundry dependence with NVIDIA and Intel competitor and risk context
summary: This community groups reports on AMD's reliance on outside wafer foundries and assembly partners, with the competitor lists named across NVIDIA, AMD and Intel filings alongside it [0000002488-25-000012:0030][0001045810-25-000023:0013]. Most of the grouped detail comes from AMD filings, while NVIDIA and Intel contribute supplier, competitor and risk details [0000002488-26-000018:0015][0001045810-26-000021:0012][0000050863-26-000011:0062]. Intel's risks around its foundry push and capital-intensive manufacturing form a separate thread in the group [0000050863-26-000011:0061].
findings: AMD relies on TSMC for all of its wafers at 7 nm or smaller nodes and relies primarily on GF for wafers at larger nodes [0000002488-25-000012:0030].
AMD's wafer supply agreement with GF provides a minimum annual capacity allocation and sets pricing through 2026 [0000002488-25-000047:0041].

Intel says its disaggregated design approach means an interruption in tiles supplied by TSMC or another third-party foundry would leave it unable to complete assembly of products until replacement tiles are designed and sourced [0000050863-26-000011:0063].
Intel recorded $950 million in 2025 and $3.3 billion in 2024 of non-cash impairment and accelerated depreciation charges for manufacturing assets [0000050863-26-000011:0064].
NVIDIA's filing lists AMD, Huawei and Intel as competitors in accelerated computing [0001045810-25-000023:0013].

AMD's 2025 filing names Lattice Semiconductor, Microsemi, Marvell, Analog Devices, Texas Instruments and NXP as embedded-segment competitors, and the 2026 filing replaces Intel with Altera in its FPGA competitor list [0000002488-25-000012:0014][0000002488-26-000018:0014].

Under the Microsoft agreement for the Xbox, if someone offers to purchase at least 30% of NVIDIA's outstanding common stock, Microsoft may have first and last rights of refusal to purchase the stock [0001045810-25-000023:0051].

title: NVIDIA supply chain, customer concentration and strategic deals
summary: This community groups NVIDIA risk factors and related deals drawn from its 10-K and 10-Q filings, covering supply and manufacturing, customer concentration, competition, energy, cybersecurity and strategic investments [0001045810-25-000023:0020] [0001045810-26-000021:0019]. The supply-side risks center on reliance on third-party foundries and subcontractors, which reduces NVIDIA's direct control over delivery schedules [0001045810-26-000021:0025]. The community concerns NVIDIA only, and its Compute & Networking segment is named as the source of its largest customer revenue [0001045810-26-000021:0036].
findings: For fiscal year 2025, direct Customers A, B and C represented 12%, 11% and 11% of total revenue, all primarily attributable to the Compute & Networking segment [0001045810-25-000023:0035]. For fiscal year 2026, one direct customer represented 22% of total revenue and another represented 14% [0001045810-26-000021:0036].

NVIDIA says it has previously experienced manufacturing lead times of more than 12 months, and it has paid premiums, provided deposits and entered into long-term supply agreements to secure capacity [0001045810-26-000021:0019].

NVIDIA does not assemble, test or package its products and instead relies on foundries and independent subcontractors, which reduces its direct control over quantity, quality and delivery schedules [0001045810-26-000021:0025].

NVIDIA paid $13.0 billion at closing and owes $4 billion, inclusive of imputed interest, within one year under its Groq license arrangement, and it recorded $14.4 billion of goodwill from the transaction [0001045810-26-000021:0102].

NVIDIA committed $5 billion to invest in Intel Corporation, subject to regulatory approval, and reported $6.5 billion of total investment commitments as of October 26, 2025 [0001045810-25-000230:0023]. In November 2025 it agreed, subject to closing conditions, to invest up to $10 billion in Anthropic, with no assurance the investment will be completed on expected terms [0001045810-25-000230:0047].

NVIDIA states that power or water shortages, land or permitting constraints, or regulations limiting energy, water or land availability could impair customers' ability to expand data center capacity and consume its products [0001045810-25-000023:0033].

NVIDIA warns that cyber-attacks may become more prevalent and severe, and that some actors are using AI technology to launch more automated, targeted and coordinated attacks [0001045810-26-000021:0029].

title: Intel patent litigation, R2 and VLSI disputes, and European Commission matters
summary: This community groups Intel's patent suits with VLSI, R2 Semiconductor, EireOg Innovations and Media Content Protection, its European Commission competition matter, and the Spectre and Meltdown consumer class actions [0000050863-25-000109:0037][0000050863-24-000124:0035][0000050863-24-000076:0027][0000050863-25-000109:0039][0000050863-24-000076:0028]. The reports concern Intel, although the EireOg suits also accuse products with AMD CPUs [0000050863-25-000109:0039]. Several matters have produced large charges or settlements, including a $780 million R2 settlement and about $1.0 billion accrued for the VLSI litigation [0000050863-24-000149:0034][0000050863-25-000074:0033].
findings: VLSI filed three infringement suits against Intel in the Western District of Texas in April 2019, accusing various Intel processors of infringing eight patents it had acquired from NXP [0000050863-25-000109:0037].

In December 2023 the Federal Circuit reversed the infringement finding on the $675 million patent and vacated the $1.5 billion damages award on the other patent in the first Texas case [0000050863-25-000109:0037].

The Dusseldorf Regional Court found in February 2024 that Intel's processors infringe R2's patent and issued an injunction and recall order against Intel and its customers [0000050863-24-000076:0031].
In August 2024 Intel agreed to pay an aggregate $780 million under three confidential agreements with R2, Third Point and TRGP Capital [0000050863-24-000149:0039][0000050863-24-000149:0034].

In January 2022 the General Court annulled the EC's 2009 rebates findings and the €1.1 billion fine, but did not annul the EC's finding that Intel made payments to prevent sales of specific rival products [0000050863-24-000124:0031].
In September 2023 the EC imposed a €376 million ($401 million) fine on Intel based on the payments finding, and Intel has appealed the decision [0000050863-24-000149:0035].

EireOg Innovations Ltd. has filed eleven separate complaints in the Eastern and Western Districts of Texas against Intel and AMD customers, alleging that products with Intel and AMD CPUs infringe numerous patents [0000050863-25-000109:0039].

MCP sought $66 million to $398 million in royalty damages over the Philips-origin patents, but in November 2025 the court granted Intel summary judgment of invalidity of both patents, and a final judgment for Intel followed in December 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0178].

- MCP sought $66 million to $398 million in royalty damages over the Philips-origin patents, but in November 2025 the court granted Intel summary judgment of invalidity of both patents, and a final judgment for Intel followed in December 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0178].

title: AMD risk factors on competition, supply chain, tax and gray-market sales
summary: These communities are all drawn from AMD's risk-factor disclosures, covering competition from Intel and Nvidia, dependence on suppliers and outsourced partners, product and gray-market risks, tax and environmental exposures, and the ZT Systems sale [0000002488-25-000047:0032][0000002488-25-000047:0067]. The reports concern AMD only, with Intel and Nvidia appearing as competitors named in AMD's risk factors [0000002488-25-000047:0034]. AMD says dominant competitors and a small customer base could limit its market share and margins [0000002488-25-000047:0034][0000002488-25-000047:0038].
findings: AMD says many countries it does business in have implemented Pillar Two-based laws, which may materially adversely impact its provision for income taxes, net income and cash flows [0000002488-25-000047:0057].

AMD has been named a responsible party at three Superfund sites in Sunnyvale, California, and has entered into settlement agreements with other responsible parties on two of the orders [0000002488-25-000047:0059].

AMD states that Intel's rebating, allocation and pricing strategies, along with its exclusivity payments, are designed to limit AMD's market share and margins [0000002488-25-000047:0034].

A new U.S. license requirement for certain exports to China and other countries affects AMD's Instinct MI308 product, and AMD expects charges of approximately $800 million in inventory and related reserves [0000002488-25-000047:0047].

AMD warns that gray-market products may be counterfeit or substandard and can be resold to prohibited end users, and that heavily discounted gray-market products compete with its own channels and negatively impact its margins [0000002488-25-000047:0050][0000002488-25-000047:0052].

AMD's ability to innovate beyond the x86 instruction set controlled by Intel depends partly on Microsoft, and the filing states that losing Microsoft's support could materially adversely affect AMD's ability to sell its products [0000002488-25-000047:0048].
The ZT Systems manufacturing business sale is the one transaction named, and AMD says it may not find a buyer on a timely basis, on acceptable terms, or at all [0000002488-25-000047:0067].

title: AMD export controls, China licensing, joint ventures and tariffs
summary: This community centers on AMD's exposure to U.S. export controls on AI chips, especially limits on shipping Instinct integrated circuits and Versal FPGAs to China and other D5 Countries [0000002488-25-000047:0053]. The passages concern AMD only and do not describe NVIDIA or Intel [0000002488-24-000123:0059][0000002488-25-000108:0065][0000002488-25-000012:0006]. The community also links these restrictions to AMD's joint ventures, including the THATIC JV with Higon Information Technology, which was added to the Entity List in June 2019 [0000002488-25-000047:0055].
findings: Since October 2023, BIS has required a license before AMD ships certain Instinct integrated circuits and certain Versal FPGAs to China, and AMD must file a Notified Advanced Computing notification 25 days before shipping certain Versal FPGAs [0000002488-24-000123:0059].

An April 2025 license requirement on MI308 products led to approximately $800 million in inventory and related charges in the second quarter of 2025, and AMD later reversed about $360 million of those charges [0000002488-25-000108:0065][0000002488-26-000018:0042].

In August 2025 U.S. government officials expected to receive 15% of revenue from licensed MI308 sales to China, but no regulation has been published, and AMD warns such a request could lead to litigation [0000002488-26-000018:0043].

BIS announced in May 2025 that it intends to rescind the January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule and issue replacement rules that may require new export licenses and delay shipments [0000002488-25-000108:0065].

AMD warns that tariffs on data center hardware could raise costs for customers, who may delay or cancel AI infrastructure investments, which may reduce demand for its products [0000002488-26-000018:0044].
AMD's purchases from the ATMP JV were $1.7 billion in each of 2024 and 2023, and amounts payable to the ATMP JV were $476 million at December 28, 2024 [0000002488-25-000012:0104].
AMD warns it may not realize the expected benefits from the THATIC JV, including future milestone payments and royalties, given the Entity List designation [0000002488-24-000123:0069].

title: Filer CIK 0000050863 risks: debt, customers, IP litigation, Mobileye impairment and cybersecurity
summary: This community groups risk-factor disclosures from filings under CIK 0000050863, and the Intel cybersecurity report describes these as Intel's disclosures [0000050863-25-000009:0065]. Its main themes are debt and credit ratings, dividends, customer concentration, IP litigation and licensing, the Mobileye goodwill impairment, cybersecurity and leadership turnover [0000050863-25-000009:0073][0000050863-26-000011:0082]. The passages describe this one filer's risks and do not compare it with NVIDIA or AMD [0000050863-25-000009:0072][0000050863-26-000011:0085].
findings: Aggregate principal of senior unsecured notes and other borrowings fell from $51.0 billion as of December 28, 2024 to $47.2 billion as of December 27, 2025 [0000050863-25-000009:0073][0000050863-26-000011:0084].

The filer reduced and then suspended its quarterly dividend in the fourth quarter of 2024, and under its commercial CHIPS Act agreement it agreed to forgo dividends for two years [0000050863-25-000009:0073].

The three largest customers accounted for 45% of net revenue in 2024, 40% in 2023 and 42% in 2022 [0000050863-25-000009:0071]. The later filing reports them at 43% of net revenue in 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0083].

The R2 Semiconductor injunction and recall order in February 2024 could have caused significant disruption to the company's and its customers' businesses in Europe if enforced [0000050863-25-000009:0067]. The company may need to license third-party IP on terms that are not commercially reasonable, and failure to obtain such rights could preclude selling certain products [0000050863-26-000011:0081].

Participation in industry standards organizations can require the company to license patents for little or no cost, which may leave it unable to enforce certain patents against others [0000050863-26-000011:0080].

The company recorded a $2.8 billion charge in the third quarter of 2024, primarily related to Mobileye goodwill [0000050863-26-000011:0082]. A 1% increase in the discount rate would have caused an additional impairment of about $1.5 billion of the Mobileye reporting unit's goodwill [0000050863-25-000109:0061].

Intel says its Habana Labs subsidiary network was breached in the fourth quarter of 2020, and it has observed an increase in ransomware attacks in its supply chain since 2021 [0000050863-25-000009:0065].

The most recent CEO retired in December 2024 after less than four years, and a search for a new CEO was underway [0000050863-25-000009:0069]. The company has had CEO transitions in 2025, 2024, 2021 and 2019 [0000050863-26-000011:0082].

title: AMD Sunnyvale Superfund liability and privacy, AI and supply-chain compliance risks
summary: This community collects regulatory and compliance risk language on environmental cleanup, privacy and cross-border data rules, AI regulation, forced labor and cyber threats, drawn from filings under CIKs 0000002488 and 0001045810 [0000002488-24-000123:0064] [0001045810-25-000023:0048]. findings: AMD says it has been named a responsible party at three Superfund sites in Sunnyvale, California, and it remains liable for costs beyond the settlements it has reached [0000002488-25-000012:0047].

AMD warns that failing to meet customer expectations on forced and trafficked labor policies may cause customers to choose a competitor's product or lead to enforcement liability [0000002488-25-000166:0072].
Under the GDPR, penalties can reach €20 million or 4% of worldwide revenue, whichever is greater [0001045810-26-000021:0049].

The filer under CIK 0001045810 says its AI risk wording changed between the 2025 and 2026 filings, from failing to develop effective internal AI policies to failing to implement them [0001045810-26-000021:0047].

title: Intel 14A foundry dependence, fabs and product lines
summary: This community centers on Intel's 14A process node and whether it can proceed without a significant external foundry customer [0000050863-26-000011:0008]. It concerns Intel alone, with the fabs, packaging sites and product lines linked through shared process nodes such as Intel 3 and Intel 4 [0000050863-26-000011:0020]. The filings also tie these choices to a streamlined manufacturing footprint, including changes to Ireland, Ohio and Germany production [0000050863-25-000009:0014].
findings: Intel says it has few external foundry customers to date, while developing an external foundry business is a key long-term strategy [0000050863-26-000011:0008].

Intel states that if it discontinued Intel 14A and successor nodes, a majority of its products would continue to be made in its own facilities on nodes up to Intel 18A-P through at least 2030 [0000050863-26-000011:0034]. The decision to pause Intel 14A is described as potentially effectively irreversible [0000050863-25-000109:0065].
Intel says that in that case it would over time shift manufacturing for nodes beyond Intel 18A and Intel 18A-P to third-party foundries, particularly TSMC [0000050863-26-000011:0008].
Intel 18A went into high-volume manufacturing in late 2025 and is used for the first Intel Core Ultra Series 3 processor [0000050863-26-000011:0021].
Intel shifted high-volume production of its Intel 4 and Intel 3 nodes to Ireland, while the Ohio fab is being built and plans for a Germany fab are on hold [0000050863-25-000009:0014].
Intel recognized a $755 million charge in Q4 2024 for penalties it expects to pay related to Ireland SCIP construction delays [0000050863-26-000011:0068].
Intel Xeon 6 processors are manufactured on the Intel 3 node, and the Intel Core Ultra Series 1 is manufactured on Intel 4 [0000050863-26-000011:0020].
Intel launched the Gaudi 3 AI accelerators in 2024, offering significant price-performance advantages for AI inference applications [0000050863-25-000009:0012].

title: AMD debt indentures, leases and executive agreements, with Intel's Arizona Fab
summary: This community groups agreements named in AMD's exhibit indexes, including debt indentures with U.S. Bank Trust Company and Wells Fargo, a Lantana HP sublease, a Nantong Fujitsu equity purchase, and executive offer letters with a Credit Agreement [0000002488-25-000012:0138][0000002488-25-000012:0141]. title: Intel forward-looking risk factors on competition, investment, supply chain and cybersecurity
summary: This community is a set of risk factors from Intel's Form 10-Q that the company says could cause actual results to differ materially from its forward-looking statements [0000050863-24-000076:0002]. The risks center on intense competition and rapid technological change, large long-term R&D and manufacturing investments, and the complexities of developing new semiconductor products and process technologies [0000050863-24-000076:0003]. The community concerns Intel's filing alone and does not cover NVIDIA or AMD [0000050863-24-000076:0003].
findings: Intel warns that its significant long-term, inherently risky investments in R&D and manufacturing facilities may not realize a favorable return [0000050863-24-000076:0002].
Intel flags its ability to time and scale capital investments appropriately and to secure favorable alternative financing arrangements and government grants as a risk [0000050863-24-000076:0003].
The filing names its complex global supply chain as a risk, including disruptions, delays, trade tensions and conflicts, or shortages [0000050863-24-000076:0003].
Intel cites increasing and evolving cybersecurity threats, privacy risks, and potential security vulnerabilities in its products as risks [0000050863-24-000076:0003].
Intel lists its debt obligations and its ability to access sources of capital, along with fluctuations in currency exchange rates, as risks [0000050863-24-000076:0003].
The filing identifies the evolving market for products with AI capabilities and the need to attract, retain, and motivate key talent as risks [0000050863-24-000076:0003].
Intel points readers to other risks described in this report, its 2023 Form 10-K, and its other SEC filings, so this list is not exhaustive [0000050863-24-000076:0003].

title: Market-risk sensitivity: currency, interest rate, equity and commodity exposure
summary: This community covers the four market-risk categories in the Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk sections: currency exchange rates, interest rates, equity prices and commodity prices [0000050863-26-000011:0052]. The passages come from two annual filings, for the years ended December 28, 2024 and December 27, 2025, and they restate sensitivity figures for both years [0000050863-25-000009:0079][0000050863-26-000011:0052].
findings: Under a 10% weighted average adverse change in currency exchange rates, the impact on income before taxes is less than $38 million as of December 27, 2025, versus less than $54 million as of December 28, 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0052].

A 1% hypothetical rise in interest rates would raise annual interest expense by about $97 million on debt outstanding at December 27, 2025, down from $120 million at December 28, 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0052].

The fair value of marketable equity investments fell to $484 million at December 27, 2025 from $848 million a year earlier, and a 45% decline would reduce that value by $218 million [0000050863-26-000011:0053].

The marketable equity portfolio was concentrated on the Chinese Shanghai Stock Exchange Science and Technology Innovation Board at December 28, 2024, but on the New York and Hong Kong stock exchanges at December 27, 2025 [0000050863-25-000009:0080][0000050863-26-000011:0053].
Non-marketable equity investments had a carrying amount of $8.0 billion at December 27, 2025, up from $4.5 billion at December 28, 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0053].

The filings say the company operates facilities that consume commodities but is not directly affected by commodity price risk to a material degree, and it uses commodity swaps in hedging programs and sourcing plans to mitigate supplier concentration [0000050863-26-000011:0053].

title: Market risk disclosures: interest rate, equity price and foreign exchange exposure
summary: This community groups market risk disclosures covering investment and interest rate risk, publicly-held equity price risk and foreign exchange rate risk [0001045810-25-000023:0074]. The annual disclosures for fiscal 2025 and 2026 report fixed-rate senior Notes of $8.5 billion and describe foreign currency exposure as minimal [0001045810-26-000021:0073]. Sensitivity figures for interest rates, equity prices and currency movements are reported for both fiscal years, with a quarterly report for October 2025 carrying forward the same risk picture [0001045810-25-000230:0048].
findings: The fiscal 2025 annual report says a parallel shift of plus or minus 0.5% in the yield curve would change the fair value of the investment portfolio by $238 million [0001045810-25-000023:0074].
The fiscal 2026 annual report says a 0.5% decrease in the yield curve would decrease the fair value of these investments by approximately $0.2 billion [0001045810-26-000021:0073].

A hypothetical 10% decrease in publicly-held equity securities would reduce their fair value by $1.8 billion as of January 25, 2026, compared with an insignificant amount as of January 26, 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0073].
The October 2025 quarterly report puts the same equity sensitivity at $387 million [0001045810-25-000230:0048].

Direct foreign exchange exposure is described as minimal because substantially all sales are in United States dollars and foreign currency forward contracts are used to offset currency movements [0001045810-25-000023:0074].

A 10% strengthening of the United States dollar would have reduced accumulated other comprehensive income related to foreign exchange contracts by $180 million as of January 25, 2026 and by $136 million as of January 26, 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0073].

An adverse 10% foreign exchange change applied to balance sheet hedging contracts would have reduced income before taxes by $124 million as of January 25, 2026 and by $129 million as of January 26, 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0074].
A quarterly report for October 2025 states there were no material changes to the foreign exchange risks described in the prior annual report [0001045810-25-000230:0048].

title: Item 7A market risk exposures for one filer
summary: This community is the Item 7A market risk section of two annual filings from one filer, covering interest rate, default, long-term investment and foreign exchange risk [0000002488-25-000012:0079]. The later filing reports larger exposures than the earlier one, including investment holdings and forward contract notional amounts [0000002488-26-000018:0083] [0000002488-26-000018:0084].
findings: A hypothetical 50 basis-point change in interest rates would have changed the fair value of the cash equivalent and investment portfolio by about $6 million at December 28, 2024 and about $25 million at December 27, 2025 [0000002488-25-000012:0079] [0000002488-26-000018:0083].

All outstanding long-term debt carried fixed interest rates at both year-ends, so exposure to rate changes on reported interest expense was described as minimal [0000002488-25-000012:0079] [0000002488-26-000018:0083].
Default risk is limited by investing only in high credit quality securities, and all debt investments were A-rated by at least one rating agency as of December 27, 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0083].

Publicly traded equity holdings were $198 million and non-marketable equity securities and other instruments were $1.3 billion at December 27, 2025, against $0 and $468 million a year earlier, a new long-term investment risk category in the later filing [0000002488-26-000018:0083].

The notional amount of foreign currency forward contracts rose from $2.8 billion at December 28, 2024 to $3.4 billion at December 27, 2025, and the estimated net fair-value position moved from a $66 million loss to a $12 million gain [0000002488-26-000018:0084].

Foreign exchange risk arises because costs and assets and liabilities are held in foreign currencies while product sales are primarily in U.S. dollars, and derivatives are used for hedging rather than trading or speculation [0000002488-25-000012:0079] [0000002488-26-000018:0084].

title: NVIDIA interim financial statement accounting rules
summary: This community concerns NVIDIA's accounting basis for its interim financial statements, and it covers NVIDIA only, not AMD or Intel [0001045810-25-000230:0011]. It groups the GAAP and SEC rules those interim statements follow, together with their reading alongside the audited annual statements [0001045810-25-000230:0011]. It also covers a FASB income tax disclosure standard that NVIDIA is still assessing for its future annual report [0001045810-25-000230:0011].
findings: NVIDIA's unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements were prepared under U.S. GAAP for interim financial information, together with the instructions to Form 10-Q and Article 10 of SEC Regulation S-X [0001045810-25-000230:0011].

The interim statements do not include all disclosures that U.S. GAAP requires, so they must be read with the audited financial statements in NVIDIA's fiscal 2025 Form 10-K [0001045810-25-000230:0011].

In December 2023 the FASB issued an accounting standard with new and updated income tax disclosures, including disaggregation of the rate reconciliation and income taxes paid [0001045810-25-000230:0011].
NVIDIA is still assessing how adopting this FASB income tax standard will affect the disclosures in its fiscal 2026 annual report [0001045810-25-000230:0011].

title: Intel x86 and xPU product strategy
summary: This community concerns Intel's x86 architecture and its xPU product family, which Intel names as the core of its product competitiveness priority [0000050863-25-000009:0005]. Intel describes x86 as the foundation of its CPU business and xPU as a broader set of accelerators built around different workloads [0000050863-25-000009:0006].
findings: Intel describes the x86 ecosystem as the core of its business and says it has served as a foundation of modern computing for over four decades [0000050863-25-000009:0006].

Intel says it continues to advance x86 with microarchitectures focused on performance and efficiency, and in 2024 it announced an advisory group to expand the x86 ecosystem through cross-platform compatibility [0000050863-25-000009:0006].

Intel's xPU family covers client and data center GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs and other accelerators, reflecting the view that different workloads benefit from different computing architectures [0000050863-25-000009:0006].

Intel's stated product strategy is to lead and democratize compute with Intel x86 and xPU, scaling from data center to network, PCs, edge computing, AI and autonomous driving [0000050863-25-000009:0005].
